summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (L12) proposing a pre-registered experiment to test whether the sequential order of CD38 inhibitor (CD38i) and NAD precursor administration produces asymmetric residual tissue ΔNAD after documented senescent-cell/SASP clearance. The claim is currently NEGATIVE/UNKNOWN — no matched head-to-head (H2H) sequential order experiment has been performed. The document is a research-discussion proposal, not a report of completed experiments.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim (Hypothesis L12)
content_blocks.content: After documented senescent-cell/SASP clearance, residual tissue ΔNAD from a matched CD38-inhibitor-then-NAD-precursor sequence differs from residual tissue ΔNAD from the reverse precursor-then-CD38-inhibitor sequence at matched total exposure. This is a pre-registered order-asymmetry H2H hypothesis after matched senolytic/SASP run-in. The claim is explicitly UNKNOWN — no experiment has been run to confirm or refute it.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Subtract-before-add framework: clear SASP-driven CD38+ macrophage load first, then run two sequential arms (CD38i→precursor vs precursor→CD38i) at matched total exposure and score residual tissue ΔNAD. Key mechanistic priors: (1) CD38 gates age-related NAD decline and NMN fate in vivo; (2) SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that drain tissue NAD; (3) senescent/SASP ablation lowers CD38 and partially restores NAD via an NMN-dependent ecto-block route; (4) 78c-class CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy. Incomplete clearance/residual CD38+ load can interact with which lever hits first — this interaction is predicted, not measured.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
Four key literature references cited as mechanistic priors (none constitute the proposed order H2H experiment):
1. PMID 27304511 (Camacho-Pereira 2016, Cell Metab): Age NAD↓ requires CD38; CD38 gates NMN fate in vivo. Role: CD38–NAD/NMN-gating prior for residual assays.
2. PMID 33199924 (Covarrubias 2020, Nat Metab): SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that reduce tissue NAD. Role: subtract-before-add / incomplete-clearance motivation; not an order panel.
3. PMID 33199925 (Chini 2020, Nat Metab): Senescent/SASP ablation ↓CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD via NMN-dependent process. Role: post-clearance baseline prior, not CD38i↔precursor order H2H.
4. PMID 35263032 (Tarragó 2022, Aging Cell): CD38i 78c increases lifespan/healthspan in chronological aging. Role: monotherapy tool prior, not order panel after senolysis.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Disciplinary Constraints
content_blocks.content:
1. L5–L11 cards (ranking/stack surplus/absolute-vs-fractional duals) do NOT prove L12 — they never ran matched CD38i→precursor vs precursor→CD38i residual ΔNAD after clearance; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated order asymmetry.
2. Co-treatment ≠ order — concurrent CD38i + NR (e.g. PMID 33871064) or synergistic-stack reviews do not report sequential residual arms after matched senolytic/SASP run-in.
3. Incomplete clearance/target-load can interact with order; Chini clearance/ecto-block and 78c monotherapy are not order panels; L9 stack surplus ≠ temporal-order H2H; no dosing specified.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: The hypothesis is refuted if: on the pre-registered order H2H residual panel after verified clearance, residual_CD38i_then_precursor falls inside the equivalence band of residual_precursor_then_CD38i (order equivalence), when CD38↓ is verified — especially under incomplete clearance, exposure mismatch, or when apparent asymmetry is only an assay-definition artifact under the pre-registered residual definitions.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design (Method)
content_blocks.content: Method type: propose-assay (NOT YET EXECUTED). Design: (1) Senolytic/SASP run-in with documented clearance verified by CD38 activity + SC/SASP markers; (2) Arm A: CD38i (78c-class) then NAD precursor (NMN/NR-class) at matched total exposure; (3) Arm B: NAD precursor then CD38i at matched total exposure; (4) Readout: residual tissue ΔNAD ± CD38 activity. Tissue targets to be locked (WAT/liver suggested). Pre-registration of α/N required before claiming order asymmetry. No dosing specified.

key_findings: Hypothesis L12 is NEGATIVE/UNKNOWN — no matched sequential order H2H experiment (CD38i→precursor vs precursor→CD38i after senolytic/SASP clearance) has been performed; execution_status=NOT_RUN.
Soft-complete literature search found zero papers matching the intersection of order∩CD38i∩precursor∩senolytic for a sequential residual ΔNAD panel.

Four mechanistic literature priors support the biological plausibility: CD38 gates age NAD/NMN fate (PMID 27304511), SASP induces CD38-high macrophages draining tissue NAD (PMID 33199924), clearance reduces CD38 and partially restores NAD via NMN-dependent ecto-block (PMID 33199925), and 78c CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (PMID 35263032).
Critical disciplinary constraint: co-treatment (concurrent CD38i + NR) is explicitly NOT equivalent to sequential order H2H; L5–L11 ranking/dual/stack-surplus cards do not prove order asymmetry.
Proposed assay requires: verified senolytic/SASP run-in, matched total exposure for both arms, pre-registered equivalence band and α/N, and locked tissue (WAT/liver) before any order-asymmetry claim.
Estimated time to refute: 6 weeks at kill cost tier 2; IP class is subtract-before-add; FTO status unknown.
The project is at TRL 1 — concept/hypothesis only, with no experimental data generated; all supporting evidence is from third-party literature.
